published_statement: Vilenkin, verbatim. Scope, abstract p.852: 'The gravitational properties of vacuum domain walls and strings are studied in the linear approximation of general relativity. These properties are shown to be very different from those of regular massive planes and rods.' The string source, p.853: 'Consider a static string parallel to the z axis. ... and assuming that all the fields phi^(i) are functions only of x and y, we find that T~^0_0 = T~^3_3 (9) and that all other components are equal to zero ... Thus, the energy-momentum tensor of the string is given by T~^nu_mu(x,y) = mu delta(x-a) delta(y-b) x diag(1, 0, 0, 1), (11) where mu is the linear energy density.' Linearised equations, p.853 eq.(14): '(nabla^2 - d_t^2) h_mu nu = 16 pi G (T_mu nu - 1/2 eta_mu nu T)'. The general massive string, p.854 eq.(20): 'h_00 = h_33 = 4G(mu + p) ln(r/r_0), h_11 = h_22 = 4G(mu - p) ln(r/r_0). Here p is the pressure in the z direction ... For a vacuum string, p = -mu and h_00 = h_33 = 0, h_11 = h_22 = 8 G mu ln(r/r_0). (21)'. The cone, p.854 eqs.(27)-(33): 'ds^2 = dt^2 - dz^2 - (1 - lambda)(dr^2 + r^2 dphi^2), (27) where lambda = 8 G mu ln(r/r_0). (28) Introducing a new radial coordinate r' as (1 - lambda) r^2 = (1 - 8 G mu) r'^2, (29) (1 - lambda) dr^2 = dr'^2, (30) we get ds^2 = dt^2 - dz^2 - dr'^2 - (1 - 8 G mu) r'^2 dphi^2. (31) With a new angular coordinate phi' = (1 - 4 G mu) phi, (32) the metric takes a Galilean form ... (33) This metric, however, does not describe a Euclidean space, since phi' changes from 0 to (1 - 4 G mu) 2 pi. Such space can be called conical.' and eq.(34): 'Thus the light deflection is delta phi = 4 pi G mu and is independent of the impact parameter rho.' Exact solution, p.856: 'there exists an exact static solution which matches with the weak-field approximation (33). It is just the locally flat "conical" space (33) with 0 < phi' < (1 - 4 G mu) 2 pi.' ... 'The metric (41) can be matched with the weak-field approximation (33) only if K - 1 = O(G^2 mu^2). Inside the string (r <~ r_0), T^nu_mu != 0 and the metric is different from (33) or (41). If we assume that gravitation does not break the Lorentz invariance of the string in the z direction, then the only allowed values of K in Eq. (41) are K = 1 and K = -3. ... K = 1 corresponds to a conical space.' The number '8 pi G mu' is not printed by Vilenkin as a deficit; it is the arithmetic 2 pi - (1 - 4 G mu) 2 pi of his eq.(33) range (reaudit V3). Hindmarsh & Kibble (READ, hep-ph/9411342 p.53) print it: 'the angular coordinate running from 0 to 2 pi - delta, with delta = 8 pi G mu', and p.85 eq.(6.1) 'delta = 8 pi G mu'.
published_hypotheses: READ (Vilenkin abstract, p.852): the LINEAR approximation of GR ('studied in the linear approximation of general relativity'); p.853: '|h_mu nu| << 1'; harmonic gauge eq.(15).
READ (p.852-853): infinitely thin, static, straight string along z ('approximate them by infinitely thin surfaces and curves'; 'Consider a static string parallel to the z axis').

READ (p.853 eqs.9-11): for a VACUUM string T^0_0 = T^3_3 is DERIVED from 'all the fields phi^(i) are functions only of x and y' plus conservation; it is not an extra assumption for a field-theory string, but it is specific to that source. Eq.(20) is stated for a general 'massive string' with pressure p along z, and 8 G mu (hence the 8 pi G mu deficit) is obtained only at 'p = -mu' (eq.21).

READ (p.852 abstract, p.855 eq.26 context): the paper contrasts vacuum strings with 'regular massive planes and rods'; for a regular rod (p = 0) eq.(20) gives h_11 = 4 G mu ln(r/r_0), i.e. a deficit 4 pi G mu (computed, reaudit V4), not 8 pi G mu.

READ (p.856): the exact exterior is conical (K = 1) only if 'gravitation does not break the Lorentz invariance of the string in the z direction'; the string interior is not solved ('Inside the string (r <~ r_0), T^nu_mu != 0 and the metric is different'). The exact interior-exterior relation between mu and the deficit is NOT derived in this paper.

READ (Hindmarsh-Kibble p.53): 'It can be shown that the solution inside the string can be matched on to the asymptotic conical metric [161-163]. In the resulting metric, the angle deficit is no longer quite proportional to the mass per unit length, there being O(G^2 mu^2) corrections [164,165].' Refs [161-165] (Gott, Hiscock, Linet, Futamase-Garfinkle, Hindmarsh-Wray) NAMED-NOT-READ; which definition of mu carries the corrections is not settled here.

READ (Hindmarsh-Kibble p.54, eqs.4.5-4.7): for T = diag(mu,0,0,-T) delta^2 with T the tension, 'It is conical perpendicular to the string, with angle deficit 4 pi G (mu + T), but there is also a non-zero Newtonian potential' (extractor dropped the pi and mu glyphs: printed as 'angle de cit 4G ( + T )'; restored from eq.(4.6) '[1 - 2G(mu + T)]^2 R^2 dphi^2' and checked by reaudit V4).
hypothesis_drift: CONFIRMED FROM THE SOURCE (was computed only in the first audit): axial.py:130-133 'An angle DEFICIT, W'(0) < 1, is what ordinary matter makes -- that is a cosmic string, and its deficit is 8 pi G mu'. Vilenkin's eq.(20) gives the linear deficit 4 pi G (mu - p), p the axial pressure (reaudit V4, 18/18 PASS). 8 pi G mu requires p = -mu, which Vilenkin derives for the VACUUM string (eqs.9-11, 21). His 'regular massive rods' (p = 0), which is what 'ordinary matter' names, give 4 pi G mu. The owner's sentence joins 'ordinary matter' and 'cosmic string' as one thing and gives the vacuum-string coefficient to both. The coefficient is wrong for ordinary matter; the SIGN (a deficit for mu > 0) survives for any p <= mu.

CONFIRMED FROM THE SOURCE: axial.py:133 'AN ANGLE EXCESS IS THE DEFICIT OF A NEGATIVE mu' is unconditional. From Vilenkin eq.(20) an excess needs mu - p < 0: mu < 0 when p <= 0 (rod or tension), but ALSO mu > 0 with p > mu (reaudit V5: mu = 0.01, p = 0.02 gives deficit -0.1257). This is the first audit's hypothesis H2, now read at eq.(20) rather than recalled; the first audit's '4 pi G (mu + tau)' is Vilenkin's 4 pi G (mu - p) with tau = -p, and Hindmarsh-Kibble p.54 prints the same form.

UNCHANGED from the first audit, and not touched by the source: the tree's WITH_CONICAL_DEFECT (axial.py:182-183) drops the axis boundary term [W Psi'] at r = 0. Vilenkin eq.(20) gives h_33 = 4G(mu + p) ln r, so a thin string with p != -mu has Psi' ~ 2G(mu+p)/r and W Psi' -> 2G(mu + p) != 0 at the axis: the p > mu counterexample lies OUTSIDE the tree's class, exactly as the first audit computed (its D/E). Inside the class the first audit's C (deficit >= 8 pi G mu) stands; nothing read contradicts it.

SCOPE (read): Vilenkin's 8 pi G mu is a LINEARISED result with only a weak-field matching to the exact cone (p.856 'only if K - 1 = O(G^2 mu^2)'). axial.py applies it to an exact identity. The sign statement the owner draws is linear in mu at this order, so the scope difference does not flip it; the first audit's exact 8 pi G mu for uniform boost-invariant cores (its B+/B-) is a computation with mu the proper integral of u and is not contradicted by anything read, but Hindmarsh-Kibble p.53 records O(G^2 mu^2) corrections for some definition of mu (refs NAMED-NOT-READ). Recorded, not adjudicated.

DISCREPANCY IN THE CANONICAL PARAPHRASE (not the owner file), now READ: canonical.json gives W'(0) - 1 as '-8 pi G mu up to normalisation'. Vilenkin eq.(32) phi' = (1 - 4 G mu) phi gives W'(0) = 1 - 4 G mu, so W'(0) - 1 = -4 G mu (reaudit V6).

WITHDRAWN from the first audit's list: none. The first audit's IMPLICIT H3 ('mu defined through a thin limit') is confirmed as the source's own framing ('approximate them by infinitely thin ... curves', eq.8 integrates T over the cross-section).

lacked_data: Now read, not recalled: nothing in Vilenkin's deficit depends on a datum (eq.20 is kinematic linear GR; eq.12's tension estimates are orders of magnitude and do not enter). M's hypothesis (a data gap) does not apply to this result. What the source shows is a HYPOTHESIS the owner drops: the coefficient 8 pi G mu belongs to the vacuum string, p = -mu, which Vilenkin derives from the field configuration (eq.9-11) and explicitly contrasts with 'regular massive ... rods'. The owner's 'ordinary matter ... that is a cosmic string ... 8 pi G mu' merges the two cases.

grade_evidence: READ, Vilenkin PRD 23 (1981) p.854 eq.(20): 'h_00 = h_33 = 4G(mu + p) ln(r/r_0), h_11 = h_22 = 4G(mu - p) ln(r/r_0). Here p is the pressure in the z direction ... For a vacuum string, p = -mu'. The 8 pi G mu deficit (the arithmetic of his p.854 'phi' changes from 0 to (1 - 4G mu) 2 pi') holds for the vacuum string only; a regular rod has 4 pi G mu, and an axial pressure p > mu gives an excess with mu > 0 (reaudit V4-V5, 18/18 PASS). axial.py:130-135 states 8 pi G mu for 'ordinary matter' and 'AN ANGLE EXCESS IS THE DEFICIT OF A NEGATIVE mu' with neither condition, so the physics sentence is true only on a smaller class than it claims. It is not WRONG where it does work: the O4 closure (AXIS_ESCAPES_THE_SIGN = False, axial.py:193) rests on the identity with the axis term W Psi' dropped, which at first order is p = -mu (Vilenkin's h_33 ~ (mu + p) ln r), and inside that class the first audit's C (deficit >= 8 pi G mu) is not contradicted by anything read. STANDS is not available because the source attaches p = -mu to the formula and the owner does not.
